Hi Amira — thanks again for the productive discovery earlier today. Quick recap and a proposed path to get to the technical deep dive/demo: 

Summary of needs we heard
- Multi-region pilot across US, EU, APAC with predictable latency SLOs
- A 60–90 minute technical deep dive including inference cost model, prefix caching, and rollout strategy (can be split into product + infra segments)
- Compliance details (data locality, audit logs) to be covered by follow-up doc and optional SOC2 checklist call

Proposed next step: rotating demo schedule to balance time zones
- Option A (rolling weeks): Week 1 = US-friendly slot, Week 2 = EU-friendly slot, Week 3 = APAC-friendly slot, then repeat. Each session = 90 minutes (60 demo + 30 Q/A).
- Example candidate slots (all 90 mins):
  • US slot: Tue 08:30–10:00 PDT (convenient for West Coast + late EU overlap)
  • EU slot: Tue 16:00–17:30 CEST (convenient for central Europe + early APAC overlap)
  • APAC slot: Wed 09:00–10:30 SGT (APAC morning)

Operational handoff suggestion (so you meet the right presenter for your timezone):
- Redwood rotates ownership of the session each week: Ben leads the US week (architecture + runbook), Marissa leads EU week (product + integration), alternate with our on-call infra engineer for APAC week. This keeps the presenter fresh and gives your team regional continuity.

What I need from you to lock the first session:
1) Preferred approach: fixed time each week vs rotating weeks (we recommend rotating weeks for fairness)
2) Your preferred days (you mentioned Tue/Thu in the call) and up to 3 people who must attend (we'll make sure engineers are present for the first session)
3) Any hard blackout dates in the next 4 weeks

I attached an updated mutual action plan (Redwood_MAP_v2.xlsx) with candidate dates and a preliminary agenda. If that looks good I'll send a calendar series and create a HubSpot event (I put a stub link below).

Proposed start window: week of May 3rd — happy to start later if you need prep time.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Best,
